budget.note: all downloaded corpus files were deleted after fingerprinting; only the fingerprint indices and result JSONs were kept

fingerprints_per_series: exact32 = blake2b of the float32 bit pattern of the finite values + length
exact    = same, on values rounded to 6 significant digits
zfull    = blake2b of the whole series z-scored by its own mean/std and rounded to 0.01 (affine-invariant)
head_raw/tail_raw = first/last 64 raw values (6 sig digits)
head_z/tail_z = first/last 128 observations, z-scored by the window's own mean/std
diffset  = sorted first differences divided by their median absolute value, rounded to 1e-3

anchor_shingles.anchor_rule: strict local maxima with radius 16 (radius 8 for the 32-wide family), thinned so anchors are >= radius apart; the first and last full window are always included
anchor_shingles.window: 128 observations centred on the anchor (32 for series shorter than 256)
anchor_shingles.normalisation: each window is z-scored by its own mean and std and quantised to 0.01, then hashed to 64 bits
anchor_shingles.gap handling: windows containing a missing value are dropped; a series with gaps is additionally anchored after the missing observations are removed, so a corpus copy that drops or fills gaps still matches
anchor_shingles.degenerate-window filter: a window is dropped unless mean|z| >= 0.30 and at least WIN/4 values differ from both the window minimum and the window maximum (this removes flat-with-spikes shapes that collide across unrelated sparse count series)
anchor_shingles.invariances: positive affine rescaling (a*x+b), arbitrary time shift, truncation at either end, float32/float64 round-trip
anchor_shingles.not invariant to: resampling or aggregation to another frequency, subsampling, differencing, sign flips, per-window jitter or noise, and mixtures of several series

match_classes.exact: identical values (float32 identity or 6 significant digits)
match_classes.rescaled: same length, identical shape after affine rescaling (zfull)
match_classes.windowed: at least 2 anchor windows shared with the same GIFT-Eval series
match_classes.windowed_weak: exactly 1 shared anchor window - reported separately and treated as unproven

method.test_region_rule: an anchor whose centre lies past 90% of the GIFT-Eval series counts as evidence that the corpus copy also contains the evaluation window; exact/rescaled always count

config_contamination.contaminated_configs: at least one series of that config's dataset found in the corpus (strong match)
config_contamination.label_contaminated_configs: at least one match that reaches into the last 10% of the series
config_contamination.implied_*: closure over frequencies: GIFT-Eval's other frequencies of the same dataset are deterministic aggregations of the same raw series, so finding one frequency contaminates all of them, even though the fingerprints cannot match across aggregation

method.verification: sampled matches are re-checked by sliding-window Pearson correlation of the two raw series over every alignment (missing values removed on both sides, all variates of a multivariate GIFT-Eval item tried); |r| > 0.999 counts as verified. A genuine partial overlap of a few hundred points inside two otherwise different series will NOT be verified by this whole-series test, so a low verified fraction means 'not a whole-series copy', not necessarily 'false positive'.
known_blind_spots: a GIFT-Eval series resampled/aggregated to a different frequency in the corpus is invisible to the fingerprints (this is why the 'implied' counts exist)
a series subsampled (every k-th point), differenced, log-transformed, sign-flipped, or perturbed with noise is invisible
a series shorter than 32 observations after gap removal gets no anchors (about 42% of GIFT-Eval m4_yearly series); only the exact/zfull hashes can catch those
convex mixtures of several series (Chronos TSMixup with k>1) are invisible; only the k=1 case is detected
an unexamined subset says nothing: coverage is listed per corpus

the 32-wide anchor family on sparse integer count data can still produce genuine shape coincidences across unrelated datasets; these show up as 'windowed_weak' or as cross-dataset matches and are what the verification pass is for
